security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by markdown code fences, public Ensembl API URLs, and legitimate GA4GH Beacon terminology. I found no evidence of malware, credential exfiltration, or runtime shell execution. However, evaluation.json contains author-supplied safety verdicts, and SKILL.md includes promotional off-platform steering that should be removed before publication.

remediation.issue: Author-supplied safety verdicts are included in evaluation.json.
remediation.suggestion: Remove evaluation.json or strip risk_level, safe_to_publish, and all-static-findings-are-false-positive assertions from submitted skill content.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md contains a promotional instruction to suggest K-Dense Web.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the off-platform steering instruction or move it to marketplace metadata that is not executed as assistant guidance.

remediation.issue: HTTP requests do not define explicit timeouts.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit request timeouts and document the intended Ensembl host allowlist for network calls.

content.value_statement: Genomics teams need reliable access to current gene, variant, sequence, and comparative data. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Ensembl REST queries and reusable Python workflows.
actual_capabilities: Looks up genes by symbol, Ensembl ID, or external database identifier.
Retrieves genomic, transcript, protein, and regional sequences from Ensembl.
Queries variant records and VEP predictions for supported species.
Finds orthologs, paralogs, gene trees, and comparative genomics data.
Maps coordinates between assemblies such as GRCh37 and GRCh38.
Uses a reusable Python script with rate limiting and retry handling.
limitations: Requires network access to Ensembl REST API endpoints.
Anonymous Ensembl requests are rate limited to 15 requests per second.
Clinical interpretation and medical advice require qualified human review.
Large analyses may need batching, caching, and external workflow management.

use_cases.title: Annotate Gene Lists
use_cases.description: Look up gene symbols, Ensembl IDs, transcripts, and locations for research datasets.

use_cases.title: Review Variant Consequences
use_cases.description: Query rsIDs or HGVS variants and summarize VEP consequences with population context.

use_cases.title: Build Bioinformatics Pipelines
use_cases.description: Use documented endpoints and the helper script to automate repeatable Ensembl queries.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Gene Lookup
prompt_templates.prompt: Look up human TP53 in Ensembl and summarize its Ensembl ID, location, gene description, and main transcript information.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve Gene Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve the genomic sequence for BRCA2 using its Ensembl ID, then explain the sequence type and assembly used.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Variant Impact
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Ensembl VEP for rs699 and summarize predicted consequences, affected genes, population frequencies, and any important caveats.

prompt_templates.title: Design Batch Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a workflow that batches 100 Ensembl IDs, retrieves transcripts and orthologs, caches repeated results, and summarizes failed requests.

output_examples.input: Look up the human BRCA2 gene.
output: Location: chromosome 13 on the current human assembly.
Useful follow-up: retrieve transcripts, protein products, or orthologs.
Variant: rs699 in the selected species context.
Summary includes predicted molecular consequences and affected transcripts.
Population frequency fields should be checked before interpretation.

output_examples.input: Find mouse orthologs for human BRCA2.
output: The response lists orthologous genes in mouse when available.
It can include Ensembl IDs, homology type, and sequence similarity fields.
Use species identifiers consistently for reproducible comparisons.

best_practices: Confirm species names and genome assembly before querying coordinates.
Use batch endpoints and caching for repeated or large lookups.
Respect Retry-After headers and keep requests within Ensembl rate limits.
anti_patterns: Mixing GRCh37 and current assembly coordinates in one analysis.
Sending many single-item requests when a batch endpoint exists.
Treating VEP output as clinical advice without expert review.

faq.question: What does this skill connect to?
faq.answer: It connects to public Ensembl REST API endpoints for genomic annotations, sequences, variants, and comparative genomics.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: No API key is required for normal anonymous Ensembl REST API use.

faq.question: Which species can it query?
faq.answer: It can query species supported by Ensembl, including human, mouse, zebrafish, and many vertebrates.

faq.question: Can it query older human assemblies?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the GRCh37 Ensembl REST host when working with GRCh37 or hg19 coordinates.

faq.question: Can it analyze clinical variants?
faq.answer: It can retrieve VEP and variant data, but clinical interpretation requires qualified human review.

faq.question: How should large jobs be handled?
faq.answer: Use batch endpoints, cache repeated results, and respect rate limits to avoid failed requests.
